source_text: IX. Altera die post hanc visionem expectantes eramus horam illam, quando fiscalis, non cibus, sed penuria et necessitas inferretur; quia cibus nullus nobis suberat, nam et altera die ieiuni manseramus. [Sicut?] autem ut sitientibus potus, esurientibus cibus, desiderantibus martyrium obvenit, ita laboribus nostris refrigerium dominus per Lucianum carissimum nobis praebuit, qui disrupto catenarum durissimo obice, velut per duas fialas, per Herennianum hypodiaconum et Ianuarium catecuminum alimentum indeficiens omnibus ministravit. hoc subsidium aegros et laborantes nimium suffulsit: eos quoque qui per eundem laborem, hoc est per incommodum solonis et frigidae aquae, aegritudinem iam inciderant, ab infirmitate revocavit. cuius tam gloriosis operibus omnes apud deum gratias agimus.
thought_title: Food supplied in prison after hunger
orientation: The imprisoned letter writers report how their hunger and thirst after the vision of the bowls were relieved through fellow Christians.
pass_a_gloss: On the next day after this vision we were expecting that hour, when prison allowance, not food, but want and need would be brought in; because no food remained to us, for also on the other day we had remained without eating. But just as as to those thirsting drink, to those hungering food, to those desiring it martyrdom falls to them, so to our toils the Lord through dearest Lucian furnished relief to us, who with the hardest barrier of the chains broken through, as through two bowls, through Herennian the subdeacon and Januarius the person preparing for baptism served to all nourishment not failing. This support strongly held up the sick and those toiling greatly: those also who through the same toil, that is through the discomfort of salt and of cold water, had already fallen into sickness, it called back from weakness. For his works so glorious we all give thanks before God.

choices.why: context is what is carried into prison at the hour, contrasted with cibus and explained as penuria
locked brief glossary requires this English for catecuminus
answer to laboribus, parallel to drink for thirst and food for hunger, not coolness
literal propping of the sick and exhausted by aid, not general comfort

pass_b_english: The next day after this vision we waited for the hour when the prison allowance would be carried in, and it was no food but want and need. We had no food left at all, for we had gone without eating the day before as well.

But as drink comes to the thirsty, food to the hungry, and martyrdom to those who long for it, so the Lord gave relief to our toils through our dearest Lucian. He broke through the hardest barrier of chains and, as if through two bowls, served unfailing nourishment to us all through Herennian the subdeacon and Januarius, a person preparing for baptism. That help held up the sick and those utterly worn out, and it even called back from weakness those who had already fallen ill through that same hardship, that is through the misery of the bare floor and the cold water. For his most glorious works we all give thanks before God.
notes: [Sicut?] is editorial uncertainty in the source; glossed as just as with doubt
solonis is uncertain; glossed as of salt without inventing salt water
altera die occurs twice; gloss keeps next day and other day as written
